evidence: Cic. Sen. 46: quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit
Liv. 21.33.6: quōs nemora etiam repercussaeque vallēs augēbant
terms.comment: Transitive; in the passive, “to increase, grow”.

evidence: Liv. 3.26.4: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia
terms.comment: Of what grows or increases by itself.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 52: vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta

phrases.latin: habeōque senectūtī magnam grātiam, quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit, pōtiōnis et cibī sustulit
phrases.english: and I am very grateful to old age, which has increased my appetite for conversation and taken away my appetite for food and drink

phrases.latin: crēvit ex metū aliēnō, ut fit, audācia
phrases.english: as usually happens, their boldness grew with the other side’s fear
